rows.note: Use this all-purpose verb when liquid splashes or is splashed onto a person or surface.

example.english: Be careful—the wet road may splash you when cars go past.
example.traditional: 小心啲，地下濕滑，車經過會濺到你。
example.jyutping: siu2 sam1 di1 dei6 haa6 sap1 waat6 ce1 ging1 gwo3 wui5 zin3 dou3 nei5

rows.note: Use this when someone deliberately splashes water around while playing or bathing.

example.english: At the beach, we splash water at each other and can't stop laughing.
example.traditional: 我哋喺沙灘玩水，成日互相撥水，笑到停唔到。
example.jyutping: ngo5 dei6 hai2 saa1 taan1 waan2 seoi2 seng4 jat6 wu6 soeng1 but6 seoi2 siu3 dou3 ting4 m4 dou3

rows.note: Use this for the loud boom or crash heard when something hits water.

example.english: The stone hit the water with a loud splash.
example.jyutping: go3 sek6 zai2 dit3 lok6 seoi2 gwang1 jat1 seng1

rows.note: Use this for a small amount of liquid, especially in everyday speech.

example.english: Just add a splash of water to the cup noodles.
example.jyutping: bui1 min6 gaa1 siu2 siu2 seoi2 zau6 gau3 laa3

rows.note: Use this when an event attracts widespread attention or causes a sensation.

example.english: This news made a splash as soon as it came out.
example.traditional: 呢單新聞一出就轟動晒。
example.jyutping: ni1 daan1 san1 man4 jat1 ceot1 zau6 gwang1 dung6 saai3

rows.note: Use this for a small splash or patch of colour on a surface.

example.english: There is a splash of colour on the white wall that will not come off.
example.traditional: 白牆上有一撻色，點都抹唔甩。
example.jyutping: baak6 coeng4 soeng6 jau5 jat1 taat3 sik1 dim2 dou1 maat3 m4 lat1
